### Problem: Majority Element II {#sec-hash-p4-b}

::: {.p-statement}
Given $a$ ($1 \le n \le 5 \cdot 10^4$, $-10^9 \le a_i \le 10^9$), return *all* values that appear more than $\lfloor n/3 \rfloor$ times, **in any order**. No existence guarantee this time.

Source: [LC 229 · Majority Element II](https://leetcode.com/problems/majority-element-ii/){.solved difficulty="Medium"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
More than $n/3$ admits **two** winners, so two counters — and the general rule: threshold $n/(k{+}1)$ needs $k$ counters, because the deletion batch is now "$k{+}1$ mutually distinct elements", each batch taking at most one copy from any value that clears the bar (@sec-hash-vote). One more thing changes: nothing promises that a winner exists. Every value above $n/3$ is guaranteed to end in a seat, but a seat may also hold a value that never reached the threshold — on $[1, 2, 3]$ the seats end holding $1$ and $2$, and neither occurs more than once. So the verification pass is part of the algorithm, not a courtesy: it removes the impostors.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Count everything.** `Counter`, keep every key with count $> n/3$. The honest baseline; $O(n)$ space.
2. **Two-counter voting, then verify.** Run the $k=2$ cancellation chain (match slot 1, match slot 2, else fill an empty slot, else burn one of each), then count the at-most-two survivors against the array. $O(n)$ time, $O(1)$ space.

**Invariant.** After any prefix, the two counters count the "standing" copies of the two seated values, and every other element of the prefix has been removed in a triple of three *different* values. A value with more than $n/3$ copies cannot be removed completely, because each triple takes at most one of its copies and there are at most $n/3$ triples — so it always holds a seat at the end. Verification then removes seated values that are below the threshold.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Histogram, filtered by the threshold

::: {.form-next}
$\{v : \text{count}[v] > \lfloor n/3 \rfloor\}$ read straight off a `Counter`. The set has size at most two — two values can each exceed a third — so the *answer* is tiny even though the histogram is $O(n)$.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
from collections import Counter

def majority_ii_counter(a):
    cnt = Counter(a)
    return sorted(v for v, c in cnt.items() if c > len(a) // 3)
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
#include <unordered_map>
using namespace std;

vector<int> majorityElementIICounter(vector<int>& a) {
    unordered_map<int, int> cnt;
    for (int x : a) ++cnt[x];
    vector<int> out;
    for (auto& e : cnt)
        if (e.second > (int)a.size() / 3) out.push_back(e.first);
    sort(out.begin(), out.end());          // our convention; LC accepts any order
    return out;
}
```
:::

#### Two counters, then a mandatory verify

::: {.form-next}
Extend @sec-hash-p4-a's leaderboard to two seats. A value matching a seat reinforces it; a newcomer takes an empty seat; a newcomer when both seats are held burns one of *each* (the "three distinct vanish" batch). Then — the step that separates this from 169 — recount both survivors over the array and keep only the ones truly above $n/3$.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("majority2", "vote2")
    assert str(final) == "[1, 3]"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: arr-majority-element-ii
def majority_ii_vote(a):
    c1 = c2 = None
    n1 = n2 = 0
    for x in a:
        if c1 is not None and x == c1:   n1 += 1   # matches seat 1
        elif c2 is not None and x == c2: n2 += 1   # matches seat 2
        elif n1 == 0: c1, n1 = x, 1                # seat 1 empty: adopt
        elif n2 == 0: c2, n2 = x, 1                # seat 2 empty: adopt
        else: n1 -= 1; n2 -= 1                     # three distinct: burn one each
    cnt = Counter(a)                               # VERIFY - part of the algorithm
    return sorted(v for v in {c1, c2}
                  if v is not None and cnt[v] > len(a) // 3)


for _ in range(3000):
    a = [random.randint(1, 4) for _ in range(random.randint(1, 12))]
    assert majority_ii_vote(a) == majority_ii_counter(a)

assert majority_ii_vote([3, 2, 3]) == [3]                  # the LC examples
assert majority_ii_vote([1, 1, 1, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2]) == [1, 2]
assert majority_ii_vote([1, 2]) == [1, 2]                  # both clear n/3 = 0
assert majority_ii_vote([0, 0]) == [0]
assert majority_ii_vote([1, 2, 3]) == []                   # seats hold 1 and 2: both impostors
assert majority_ii_vote([1, 1, 2, 2, 2]) == [1, 2]         # needs "match a seat" tested first
assert majority_ii_vote([1, 2, 2, 3, 1, 3, 1, 3]) == [1, 3]  # the board sample
print("majority_ii OK")
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr);
    int n; cin >> n;
    vector<int> a(n);
    for (int& x : a) cin >> x;                 // keep it: verify needs a second pass
    int c1 = 0, c2 = 0, n1 = 0, n2 = 0;        // a seat with count 0 is empty; matching its
    for (int x : a) {                          // stale value is the same as adopting x
        if (x == c1)      ++n1;
        else if (x == c2) ++n2;
        else if (n1 == 0) { c1 = x; n1 = 1; }
        else if (n2 == 0) { c2 = x; n2 = 1; }
        else { --n1; --n2; }                   // three distinct values vanish
    }
    vector<int> out;                           // the verify pass: recount both survivors
    for (int c : {c1, c2}) {
        int real = (int)count(a.begin(), a.end(), c);
        if (real > n / 3 && find(out.begin(), out.end(), c) == out.end()) out.push_back(c);
    }
    sort(out.begin(), out.end());
    for (int v : out) cout << v << '\n';
}
```
:::
:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Histogram, filtered by the threshold** is $O(n)$ expected time and $O(n)$ space — or $O(\text{range})$ with a frequency array, impossible here since values reach $\pm 10^9$. **Two counters, then a mandatory verify** is $O(n)$ time (two extra `count` scans of at most two values — still linear) and $O(1)$ auxiliary space. The generalisation prices itself the same way: threshold $n/(k{+}1)$ runs in $O(kn)$ time and $O(k)$ space, and *always* keeps the verify pass.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- The verify pass is not decoration: on $[1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 2, 2, 2]$ ($n = 9$, threshold $\lfloor 9/3 \rfloor = 3$) every value occurs exactly $3$ times, so the answer is empty — yet the seats still hold $1$ and $0$ at the end. Only recounting decides.
- $n < 3$: the threshold $\lfloor n/3 \rfloor$ is $0$, so every value that occurs qualifies; with at most two distinct values, both end in seats and both pass verification.
- Only one value ever sits down (all elements equal): the Python set `{c1, c2}` contains `None`, which the filter drops; the C++ version recounts the unused seat's value $0$, which correctly passes only if $0$ really occurs often enough.
- Test order matters: "does $x$ match a seat?" must come before "is a seat empty?". The other order can put one value in both seats and lose a real winner — on $[1, 1, 2, 2, 2]$ it would return only $[2]$ — and verification cannot bring a lost winner back.
- Order: LC accepts any; we sort so the assert on the board sample is literal.
:::

::: {.practice}
- [LC 1157 · Online Majority Element In Subarray](https://leetcode.com/problems/online-majority-element-in-subarray/){difficulty="Hard"} — majority queries on ranges: find a candidate, then verify it with the sorted list of its positions and two binary searches.
- [CF 1514D · Cut and Stick](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1514/D){rating="2000"} — the answer depends on how often a range's most frequent value occurs; random sampling of candidates plus verification by positions is one standard solution.
:::
